liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Uncle John's Band** (2 reviews): The Uncle John's, Playin', Uncle John's opener was the highlight for this reviewer; The Uncle John's, Playin', Uncle John's opening is praised, with Lesh and Garcia both standing out [18][23]
- **Tennessee Jed** (2 reviews): Tennessee Jed, along with Samson, is called reason enough to hear the show; Tennessee Jed is described as on fire [17][19]
- **Samson and Delilah** (1 review): Samson and Delilah came in the middle of the first set, which the reviewer found notable [19]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Estimated into Eyes is rated great, though the show fades somewhat afterward [17]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Second set has its moments, Eyes being one [23]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Healy reportedly left output levels mostly alone over the two days until the Sunshine Daydream section [24]
- **Alabama Getaway** (1 review): Two-song encore included a smoking Alabama Getaway [19]

## Setlist highlights

- **When Johnny Strikes Up The Band**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **Excitable Boy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [27]
- **Werewolves Of London**: back after 145 archived shows (701 days); rare: 12 archived performances [27]
- **Bob Weir Interview**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [27]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-06-08.SonyECM250.walker-scotton.miller.88452.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 26 songs; 197 min; rated 3.71/5 by 7 [1]
- **gd80-06-08.eaton.tome.7193.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 153 min; rated 4.2/5 by 10 [2]
- **gd1980-06-08.144749.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 160 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1980-06-08.155742.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 22 songs; 156 min [5]

## Around the show

- Held in the Horseshoe, with the south end of Folsom Field closed off, leaving the infield and rows of seats [15]
- Warren Zevon opened; the reviewer found the first day's crowd subdued, with Zevon's set a bright spot [15]
- Boulder had passed a decibel-limit ordinance that year; the band reportedly exceeded it the previous day during Deal [16]
- Day coincided with Parent Day, with prospective students and their families all around, unsettling parents and encouraging the kids [16]
- Recalls a helicopter over the stadium dropping baggies and joints, either at this show or the day before [18]
- Zevon reportedly gave the same set, banter and jokes as earlier days, with fans barking the punch lines [21]
- Band played from about the ten-yard line into the horseshoe, using only a fraction of the stadium [21]
- Boulder altered its decibel regulation before these shows, raising the limit for an outdoor concert to roughly jet level [24]
- Many songs repeated from the previous day, and Zevon played both days [16]
- Reviewer says no other show on the site opened with Uncle John's Band into Playin' and back into Uncle John's [17]
- Reviewer traveled from Vermont and felt let down by how many songs repeated across the two nights [18]
- Opening with Uncle John's and Playin' made it feel like the previous day never ended [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-06-08.SonyECM250.walker-scotton.miller.88452.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Sony ECM-250 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-158/Maxell UDXLII-C90) [1]. Also: Recorded by Joani Walker, sitting eight rows behind the soundboard; tapes shared via Paul Scotton [1]
- **gd80-06-08.eaton.tome.7193.sbefail.shnf**: taped by Rob Eaton; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421's [2]. Also: Recorded by Rob Eaton on Senn 421 mics into Nak 550, then DAT, CD, and SHN; Includes alternate audience patches; came through the DNC tree, Round 9, via Tome [2]
- **gd1980-06-08.144749.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics (pole mounted at the soundboard)> Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII) [3]. Also: A different audience source supplies an 11-second patch in Drums [3]
- **gd1980-06-08.155742.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; transferred by Scott Wiseman and Scott Clugston; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXL-II 90, except for Feel Like A Stranger and Ship… [5]. Also: Severson's Nakamichi 700 source fills the intro, a Drums patch, and both encores, Alabama Getaway and Brokedown Palace [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1980-06-08 Folsom Field, U. of Colorado, Boulder, CO, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1980-06-08-folsom-field-u-of-colorado-boulder-co-usa/) [28]
- Poster by Concertposterauction.com: [Grateful Dead Warren Zevon Boulder CO 1980 Concert Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/441016/Grateful-Dead-Warren-Zevon-Boulder-CO-1980-Concert-Poster) [29]

claims.text: Held in the Horseshoe, with the south end of Folsom Field closed off, leaving the infield and rows of seats
Warren Zevon opened; the reviewer found the first day's crowd subdued, with Zevon's set a bright spot
Boulder had passed a decibel-limit ordinance that year; the band reportedly exceeded it the previous day during Deal
Day coincided with Parent Day, with prospective students and their families all around, unsettling parents and encouraging the kids
Many songs repeated from the previous day, and Zevon played both days
Reviewer says no other show on the site opened with Uncle John's Band into Playin' and back into Uncle John's
Tennessee Jed, along with Samson, is called reason enough to hear the show
Estimated into Eyes is rated great, though the show fades somewhat afterward
Reviewer traveled from Vermont and felt let down by how many songs repeated across the two nights
The Uncle John's, Playin', Uncle John's opener was the highlight for this reviewer
Recalls a helicopter over the stadium dropping baggies and joints, either at this show or the day before
Samson and Delilah came in the middle of the first set, which the reviewer found notable
Tennessee Jed is described as on fire
Two-song encore included a smoking Alabama Getaway
Zevon reportedly gave the same set, banter and jokes as earlier days, with fans barking the punch lines
Band played from about the ten-yard line into the horseshoe, using only a fraction of the stadium
Opening with Uncle John's and Playin' made it feel like the previous day never ended
Follows the 15th anniversary show, which the reviewer found disappointing; this one is livelier from the start
The Uncle John's, Playin', Uncle John's opening is praised, with Lesh and Garcia both standing out
Second set has its moments, Eyes being one
Boulder altered its decibel regulation before these shows, raising the limit for an outdoor concert to roughly jet level
Healy reportedly left output levels mostly alone over the two days until the Sunshine Daydream section
Stadium was blocked off except the end zone; stage had murals of the Go to Heaven firebird
Reviewer considers this the tour that established Brent with the band
Recorded by Joani Walker, sitting eight rows behind the soundboard; tapes shared via Paul Scotton
Shows were billed as the band's 15th anniversary shows
Recorded by Rob Eaton on Senn 421 mics into Nak 550, then DAT, CD, and SHN
Includes alternate audience patches; came through the DNC tree, Round 9, via Tome
Transferred by Charlie Miller from Mark Severson's master cassettes, recorded on a Nakamichi 700
A different audience source supplies an 11-second patch in Drums
Source cassettes and transfer from Scott Wiseman, recorded with AKG mics and coordinated by Charlie Miller
Severson's Nakamichi 700 source fills the intro, a Drums patch, and both encores, Alabama Getaway and Brokedown Palace
